questions.q_en: Describe how you will say The challan shall be filled by the attendee in active voice.
options_en: The attendee shall be fill the challan.
The attendee shall fill the challan.
The attendee shall be filling the challan.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb 'be' and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in positive degree of comparison.

He was greater than any other physiologist of the century.
options_en: All other physiologists were as great as him.
He was the greatest physiologist of all.
He as a physiologist in the country was among the greatest people.
No other physiologist of the century was as great as he was.
questions.solution_en:
The positive degree of comparison is the form of an adjective or adverb that expresses a quality or condition without making any comparison. It is the base form of the word, used to describe a quality or condition as it is, without indicating that it is better or worse than anything else. Option (d) expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison by emphasising the superiority of the individual without directly comparing him to anyone else. The phrase "as great (base form) as" conveys the idea that the individual's greatness stands unmatched within the context of the century.

Option (a) is not correct. This option suggests that all other physiologists were equally great as him, which contradicts the original statement that he was greater than any other physiologist of the century.

Options (b) and (c) are not correct as they use the superlative degree (greatest), not the positive degree.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q_en: Select the most appropriate option in direct speech.
options_en: The principal say me, "You are in-charge of the admission cell."
The principal said me, You are in-charge of the admission cell.
The principal said to I, "You are in-charge of the admission cell."
The principal said to me, "You are in-charge of the admission cell."
questions.solution_en:
Option (a) is incorrect as the reporting verb 'say' is incorrect here. 'Said to' or 'says to' should have been used here. 'To' needs to be added to denote whom the principal told something ('me'). Option (b) is incorrect for the same reason.

Option (c) is incorrect as the objective pronoun 'me' should have been used in place of subjective pronoun 'I' to denote who was being told something.

Option (d) represents the correct sentence in direct speech.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Supriya found ____ interesting book at the bookstore.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is (a). The indefinite article "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. In this sentence, the word "interesting" starts with a vowel sound. So, "an" is a suitable word to use. The indefinite article "a" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound. The definite article "the" is used to specify a particular or previously mentioned noun. In this sentence, there is no prior mention or specific context to warrant the use of "the" before "interesting book." The sentence is more about a general discovery of an interesting book. It does not refer to a specific book known to both the speaker and the listener. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

A noun is a word used as the name of a person, place, or thing. Now consider the following sentences:

1) Mahesh is a clever boy.

2) A herd of cattle was grazing on the pastureland.

3) Honesty is the best policy.

An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The manager made the new intern / to stay back after office hours / to finish the urgent report.
options_en: to stay back after office hours
The manager made the new intern
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "to stay back after office hours". Certain verbs like 'make', 'let', 'help', and 'bid', when used in the active voice, are followed by a bare infinitive (the base form of a verb without 'to'). In this sentence, 'made' is used in the active voice.

Therefore, the infinitive marker 'to' should be removed before the verb 'stay'. The correct phrase is "stay back".

Correct Sentence: The manager made the new intern stay back after office hours to finish the urgent report.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

· Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

· Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.solution_en:
The indefinite article 'an' should be used before 'unexpected' primarily because it has a vowel sound. Also, 'an' is referring to an unspecified noun in the sentence, that is, 'act'.

None of the articles is used before the noun 'acts' in the second sentence because it is a plural and unspecified noun.

The sentences A, B, and D depict grammatically incorrect usage of the articles.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

King Sagara, an ancestor of King Bhagiratha, once conducted an ashwamedha yagna to extend his dominion. When the horse went astray, the king sent his 60,000 sons to find the horse. Unfortunately, in the course of the quest, they ended up disrupting the intense meditation of sage Kapila, at whose abode they found the horse. Kapila burnt them all to ashes, sending them all to the netherworld - an act he instantly regretted when he realised what had happened. After breaking the news to King Sagara, he mentioned that the souls of King Sagara's sons could attain salvation only if the heavenly Ganga could be persuaded to flow over their ashes. It was Bhagiratha, whose austere penance and devotion pleased Lord Shiva so much so that he persuaded Ganga to descend to the earth. Ganga consented, but the problem arose that the earth would probably be unable to bear the intensity of Ganga's flow and even be shattered in the process. Thus, a solution was devised: Ganga would first land on Shiva's head and the locks of his hair would minimise the impact. Still, the force of Ganga's landing was such that it split into seven tributaries, three of which flowed east and three of them west. The seventh stream followed King Bhagiratha to the place where his ancestor's ashes lay. The river's waters instantly purified them. This is also the origin of the belief that the Ganga's waters can purify mortal souls of all their sins.

This story is a:

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Fingernails and toenails helped our _________ to climb trees, peel fruits and use simple tools. While their colour and condition offer clues about your ________health. Nail polish turns them into fashion accessories.
questions.solution_en:
· For the first blank, "ancestors" is the most fitting term, as it refers to early humans or primates who used fingernails and toenails for survival tasks like climbing and tool use, which aligns with evolutionary context.

· For the second blank, "overall" is appropriate because it accurately describes the general state of health that nail color and condition can indicate, such as signs of nutritional deficiencies or medical conditions. The other options do not fit as well contextually or grammatically. For example, "predecessor" and "forefather" are less specific to evolutionary history, and "universal" or "altogether" do not convey the intended meaning for health.

The completed sentence would read: "Fingernails and toenails helped our ancestors to climb trees, peel fruits and use simple tools. While their colour and condition offer clues about your overall health. Nail polish turns them into fashion accessories."

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

"I went for a walk today morning, and met Lokesh," said Rahul.
options_en: Rahul said that he went for a walk that morning, and met Lokesh.
Rahul said that he had gone for a walk that morning, and met Lokesh.
Rahul said that I had gone for a walk that morning, and met Lokesh.
Rahul said that he had gone for a walk today morning, and met Lokesh.
questions.solution_en: The simple past tense 'went' should change into the past perfect 'had gone', when changing from direct to indirect speech. The first person subjective pronoun 'I' will change to the third person subjective 'he'. 'Today morning' will change into 'that morning'. B is the right answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

A trip to the village temple was made by Bhavani yesterday.
options_en: Bhavani was going to make a trip to the temple yesterday.
Bhavani made a trip to the village temple yesterday.
Bhavani tripped to the village temple yesterday.
Bhavani is going to make a trip to the temple today.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Subject (Objective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Object (Subjective Case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).
